content: n this case, a husband claimed reimbursement for money his parents provided for the home purchase and sought an occupancy fee from his wife,. The court had to interpret the nature of third-party contributions and the start date for occupancy indemnities,. The ruling established that money from a spouse’s parents constitutes a debt of the communion to the third party, not a personal credit of the spouse. Additionally, it was determined that the right to an occupancy fee for the exclusive use of the common home begins only when the separation judgment becomes final (res judicata).
